method: Web research on 13 Sep 2026: Pirelli press releases, FIA regulations (rulebook PDFs searched directly), formula1.com and technical press quoting Pirelli or the FIA. Only items the research marked verified are on the slides; see 'not_verified'.
title: What each rule change since 2022 did to the tyres
subtitle: Tyres, cars, fuel and sporting rules, season by season; sources in the speaker notes

seasons.headline: 18-inch tyres, ground-effect cars
changes: Rims 13 to 18 inch; diameter 660 to 720 mm
Following car loses 4% downforce at 20 m (35% in 2021)
seasons.effect: Designed to overheat less; Pirelli met most targets but saw understeer and front graining.

seasons.headline: New C1, stronger fronts
changes: New C1; the old C1 became C0
seasons.effect: Less understeer at lower pressures; the Qatar cap forced three stops.

seasons.headline: The stable year
changes: Same compounds, C0 dropped: C1 to C5
seasons.effect: No tyre change: the cleanest baseline between two rule eras.

seasons.headline: Softer range, forced stops
changes: New C6, the softest; aim of 0.5 s between compounds
Monaco: two compounds and two stops
seasons.effect: Where the tyre alone gave one stop, the rules imposed more.

seasons.headline: Smaller tyres, lighter cars, less fuel
changes: Tyres 25 mm narrower front, 30 mm rear; C6 dropped
Active aero; Overtake Mode replaces DRS
seasons.effect: Less load per lap: early one-stops, but hot Barcelona overheated tyres.

fuel.load_label: race fuel: about 100 kg (F1, 2020); 2026 target 70 kg, a target not a rule
fuel.subtitle: A lighter start hides less tyre wear in the lap times, and a lighter car loads the tyre less
facts: 2019: race fuel capped at 110 kg (2020 Sporting Regulations, Art. 30.5)
2022 to 2025: fuel mass flow limited to 100 kg/h; E10 fuel from 2022
2026: 100% advanced sustainable fuel, limited by energy flow (3,000 MJ/h) instead of mass flow; combustion engine about 400 kW, MGU-K 350 kW, MGU-H removed
2026: F1 aims for 70 kg of fuel per race against about 100 kg in 2020; no race fuel cap found in the 2026 rulebooks
Rule of thumb: about 0.3 s per 10 kg of fuel (0.03 s/kg), varying by track

not_verified: a 110 kg fuel cap in the 2022 or 2025 rulebooks (quoted by the press, not found in the rule text)
actual 2026 race-start fuel loads or per-lap burn
real 2026 downforce and drag against the FIA targets
stop counts per 2026 race from sources (ours come from the timing data)
caveats: 2022 downforce-loss figures are F1's own design numbers
2026: 768 kg is the headline figure; the rulebook states 724 kg plus tyre mass
2026 downforce and drag cuts are FIA targets, not measured values
70 kg is F1's 2026 fuel target, not a rule
